bio.p1: Civil engineer currently completing dual degrees at the Federal University of Ceará (UFC, Brazil) and INSA Rennes (France), with a research focus on pavement mechanics, materials science and numerical modeling.
bio.p2: Incoming PhD candidate at ÉTS Montréal (Canada), investigating non-destructive auscultation techniques — particularly the Falling Weight Deflectometer (FWD) — for municipal pavement evaluation, with emphasis on cold-recycled materials and freeze–thaw behavior.
bio.p3: Across research internships and industry work, I connect laboratory experimentation, field measurement and finite-element simulation to understand how road structures deform, fatigue and endure.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Research, engineering and experimental work in pavement mechanics and materials.

pavement-monitoring.title: Pavement Monitoring of Highway Structures
pavement-monitoring.summary: Structural evaluation of highway pavements using the Falling Weight Deflectometer (FWD) and deflection-basin analysis.
pavement-monitoring.description:
As part of an internship with Eiffage in Lyon, this work monitors the structural condition of highway pavements through non-destructive testing. The Falling Weight Deflectometer applies a calibrated impulse load and records the resulting deflection basin across a set of geophones.
From the measured basins, layer moduli are back-calculated and compared against design expectations, enabling data-driven decisions on maintenance and rehabilitation. Temperature corrections are applied so that measurements taken under different conditions remain comparable.

fatigue-cementitious.title: Fatigue of Cementitious Materials
fatigue-cementitious.summary: Characterizing the fatigue life of cementitious materials under cyclic loading on a UTM-25 testing press.
fatigue-cementitious.description:
Conducted within the ReoM group at UFC, this study characterizes how cementitious materials degrade under repeated loading. Specimens are tested on a UTM-25 servo-hydraulic press across a range of stress amplitudes.
The resulting stress–life (S–N) relationship is fitted with a Basquin-type power law, providing fatigue parameters that feed into pavement and structural design against cyclic damage.

ultrasonic-characterization.title: Ultrasonic Wave Characterization of Pavement Materials
ultrasonic-characterization.summary: Non-destructive characterization of pavement materials through ultrasonic wave propagation and frequency-response analysis.
ultrasonic-characterization.description:
This FUNCAP-funded project uses ultrasonic waves to probe the elastic properties of pavement materials without damaging the specimens. Wave velocities and frequency-response functions are measured and linked to the material's stiffness and internal structure.
The approach offers a fast, repeatable way to track how composition and curing affect mechanical performance, complementing destructive laboratory tests.

rheology-aam.title: Rheology of Alkali-Activated Materials
rheology-aam.summary: Investigating the creep and viscoelastic behavior of alkali-activated materials with a Burgers model.
rheology-aam.description:
Alkali-activated materials are a promising low-carbon alternative to ordinary cement. This work studies their time-dependent deformation under sustained load inside a climatic chamber.
The measured creep response is described with a four-element Burgers model, separating instantaneous, viscoelastic and viscous contributions to inform durability assessments.

thermomechanical-foundations.title: Thermomechanical Analysis of Massive Concrete Foundations
thermomechanical-foundations.summary: Modeling heat generation and the resulting thermal gradients in massive concrete foundations with ANSYS.
thermomechanical-foundations.description:
Massive concrete elements release significant heat as they cure, and the resulting thermal gradients can crack the structure. Using ANSYS, this study models transient heat transfer coupled with the mechanical response of the foundation.
The simulations map temperature fields and stress concentrations over time, supporting choices on casting sequence, cooling and mix design to limit early-age cracking.

scientific-events.summary: Organizing engineering events (Semana de Engenharia, Aqualibrium) and co-authoring an olympic-chemistry e-book.
scientific-events.description:
Beyond research, I have organized and supported scientific outreach: coordinating the Semana de Engenharia, running the Aqualibrium hydraulic-structures competition, and co-authoring an e-book on olympic chemistry.
These activities strengthened skills in communication, teamwork and event logistics while giving back to the student community.

phd.title: PhD Research — ÉTS Montréal
phd.subtitle: Non-Destructive Evaluation of Municipal Pavements
phd.description: Municipal road networks are critical infrastructure whose performance directly affects mobility. In Québec, aging pavements and harsh climatic conditions make improved diagnostic methods essential for planning rehabilitation. This project focuses on non-destructive auscultation techniques — particularly the Falling Weight Deflectometer (FWD) — to better characterize the structural behavior of municipal pavements, including cold-recycled materials (grave-emulsion, foamed bitumen). Temperature variations with depth and freeze–thaw cycles are accounted for to improve interpretation and support decision-making.
